Theme

Money, work & business · Work & responsibility

employer noun

also employers, boss, the boss

classical

Plaut. Asin. 3: gregīque huic et dominīs atque conductōribus, the troupe, its owners and those who hire it
Traupman 309: (operae) conductor, employer
Traupman 309

conductor, conductōris m.

noun, third declension

the one who hires workers: an employer

The party who condūcit, hires, labour as well as a house (see tenant); a woman is conductrīx (Traupman 309). To hire labourers, operāriōs condūcere (Cato Agr. 4).

Other words

  • dominus, dominī m. — the boss, the owner

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 282: boss (owner); Levi–Bini p. 51: principale, the head of a firm

    Classically the master of a household and its slaves, and the owner of a business (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Ille quī mē condūxit, ubi condūxit, abdūxit domum, quae voluit mihi dīxit, docuit et praemōnstrāvit prius, quō modō quicque agerem

    The man who hired me took me home the moment he had hired me; he told me what he wanted, and taught me and showed me beforehand how to do each thingPlaut. Trin. 853–855

  • Sī tē libenter vīcīnitās vidēbit, facilius tua vēndēs, opera facilius locābis, operāriōs facilius condūcēs

    If the neighbours like to see you, you will sell your produce more easily, let out your work more easily and hire labourers more easilyCato Agr. 4

See also employee, manager, director, job, wage, salary.
